question.problem: Determine the real roots of the cubic equation $12{s}^{3}+12{s}^{2}-20s=6{s}^{2}+16s.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(s)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}12{s}^{3}+12{s}^{2}-20s & =6{s}^{2}+16s \\ 12{s}^{3}+6{s}^{2}-20s & =16s \\ 12{s}^{3}+6{s}^{2}-36s & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $6s.$ We can factor out the $6s$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}12{s}^{3}+6{s}^{2}-36s & =0 \\ 6s(2{s}^{2}+s-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{s}^{2}+s-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6s(2{s}^{2}+s-6) & =0 \\ 6s(2s-3)(s+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $s=0,$ $s=\frac{3}{2},$ and $s=-2.$
